the MNDWI can be used as an effective index for water extraction in a region with a background of built up land.

the MNDWI can enhance open water information while efficiently suppressing or even removing built up and vegetation noises in remotely sensed imagery.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the MNDWI performs better than the NDWI in terms of extracting water information in a built up land background, but the NDWI performs better than MNDWI in terms of water extraction in a vegetation and/or soil background.

the MNDWI has the following advantages: (1) the water region extracted by the MNDWI contains fewer built up land pixels than that extracted by the NDWI and (2) the MNDWI can be used to efficiently extract the water information in a region with built up land areas as the background.
MNDWI is superior to the NDWI in extracting and enhancing open water features when the background of the study area is dominated by built up lands.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the MNDWI has a better ability to extract water information than the NDWI for a water region in which built up land noise is dominant.

the NDWI can be used for enhancing and extracting open water information for a background dominated by vegetation and soil areas while the MNDWI can be used to enhance and extract open water information for background dominated by built-up land areas.
the MNDWI can enhance and extract open water features in a water region with built up land areas and the NDWI can enhance open water and built up land features in a waterless region.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the MNDWI can be applied to improve the extraction and monitoring of water bodies in a region with a background of built up land.
the MNDWI can be used for water feature extraction in a water region with built up land background and can provide a better result in comparison with NDWI.
